text:
A: Hiya! Oh, there you are. Can you hear me alright, love?
B: Hi, yeah, yeah, perfectly. Sorry, my screen froze for a sec. Hi. I'm Matthew.
A: Leanne. I'm in Castleford, West Yorkshire. Where are you?
B: Norwich. Well, I grew up in Lowestoft, but I've been in Norwich a while now.
A: Ooh, by the coast. Lovely. Did you do that puzzle at the start? I were rubbish at it. I was sat there going, I don't know what they want me to do here.
B: Ha, yeah, I sort of got there in the end, but I wouldn't swear it was right. I was quite pleased with myself and then I thought, hang on.
A: That's me with every quiz. We do a pub quiz Thursdays with work and I'm always dead confident and always wrong. So what is it you do then?
B: Erm, it's, er, it sounds more exciting than it is. I do flood risk modelling. So basically computer models of rivers, really. If someone wants to build houses near a river, or the Environment Agency's planning a flood defence, I work out where the water would go, how deep, that sort of thing. Then I try and explain it to people in plain English, which is the hard bit, honestly.
A: Oh, that's not boring at all! We've had flooding round here, you know. Castleford's right where the Aire and the Calder meet. Me mum's friend got flooded out years back and she still talks about it. Every time it rains for three days she's on the phone.
B: Yeah, that's exactly the kind of place. Confluences are always, er, a bit of a headache. And it's the people that stick with you, you know, the ones who've been flooded, it never really leaves them.
A: No, it doesn't. Sorry, I'm rambling, aren't I. You go on, ask me something.
B: No, no, not at all, honestly. Erm, what do you do?
A: I'm on a packing line at a food factory. I run a flow-wrap machine, and I'm the trainer, so all the new starters and the agency lot get put with me. I like that bit, I like having a laugh with them. I'm part-time though, three shifts, so I've got time for me mum and choir and that.
B: Oh, you sing? That's brilliant.
A: Alto! Community choir. We're rehearsing for Christmas already, in October, can you believe it. Do you sing?
B: God, no. Well, in the car. Badly. I go to a lot of gigs though, at the Waterfront mostly, indie stuff. Got one next month actually.
A: I saw your poster behind you! I thought, he's into his music, him. I'm more musicals. Wicked, Mamma Mia, I cried at both.
B: Honestly, I cried at a Pixar film in the cinema, so no judgement here.
A: Which one?
B: Erm, Coco. The bit with the grandma. Sorry, spoiler, but it's been out years.
A: Oh, don't. I'm welling up just thinking about it. My dad... well, anyway. Ha. See, I'm getting emotional and we've only been talking two minutes.
B: No, that's fine, honestly. It gets everyone. My nan used to... yeah. It's a good film.
A: It is. Right, cheer up, what are you having for your tea tonight?
B: Chilli. I made way too much on Sunday and keep forgetting to freeze it, so it's chilli until it runs out.
A: Same as me with stew! A big pan does me three days. Have you got
B: Sorry, go on.
